health_check.note: #892/#894 — replaces a log-tail probe that decided health from the last log line's timestamp alone, so the producer's own `logger.error(...)` failure line (freshly timestamped) read as a fresh healthy marker — the check inverted under the exact failure it existed to detect. The pointer is written by scripts/obsidian/sync-heartbeat.py on EVERY exit path, including the sync-process-down early return (`sys.exit(2)`) — that path is exactly when the pointer matters most. heartbeat_age_minutes.reason: Informational age of the vault heartbeat file at check time. completed_at_utc is the freshness anchor for this pointer's OWN staleness; this measures a different thing (the monitored file's age), not the pointer's.

What the ledger cannot express is the *why* behind two good-sets, preserved here because a future reader without this context could plausibly "simplify" them into each other. restic_exit_code accepts {0, 3} because a backup exiting 3 completed with warnings but still produced a snapshot; prune_exit_code accepts only {0} because restic forget exiting 3 means snapshots could not be removed, which is not a successful retention pass -- merging the two good-sets is a named prior regression (#902). 127 is the script's 'never attempted' sentinel for both steps and is unhealthy for both. script_finished_at_utc is diagnostic_only and must never become a freshness fallback: it was one, and a run producing no snapshot once read fresh through it (#902/FR-009) -- the anchor is snapshot_timestamp_utc alone. A prune failure makes this component unhealthy but deliberately does NOT gate Tier-2 deploys: scripts/deploy/lib/snapshot.py reads only restic_exit_code and the snapshot timestamp, because a failed prune does not invalidate the snapshot. Prune failure alerts; it does not block.

See docs/runbooks/restic-backup-ops.md. #902: prune_exit_code added to the pointer -- previously a prune failure was logged as a WARNING and discarded, so a stale lock blocked retention for ten hours while every health surface correctly reported the BACKUP healthy. pointer-key-ledger-01M189P6/WP01 added last_integrity_check_utc, files_processed, source_roots_present, and repo_fs_free_bytes (schema v1 -> v2).

services.purpose: Detection half of the Felix Truthful Reporting Guardrails (kentonium3/kg-automation#683). Each tick runs three deterministic scans and alerts via the #701 unified alert bus (felix-alert topic; C-002, no parallel channel): (1) cron-drift detection — diffs live OpenClaw crons (`openclaw cron list --json`) against the committed approved-cron baseline (approved-crons.json), the load-bearing agent-independent guard against unrequested standing infrastructure (FR-003/FR-005/FR-006(b)); (2) completion-assertion verification — checks artifact ids named in completion-assertion ledger records (auto-emitted by artifact-creation helpers, e.g. the Vikunja task helper) against their owning system, grounding completion claims (FR-004/FR-005/FR-006(a)). (3) deployed-unit-vs-repo drift detection (kentonium3/kg-automation#817) — diffs each deployed systemd-user unit against its repo canonical (globbed from scripts/office2, scripts/openclaw/deploy, scripts/sync/systemd, scripts/deploy/felix-deployer), functional-content-normalized (comments/whitespace ignored), catching the #816 class of a stale deployed unit (ExecStart/PYTHONPATH) that fails silently; openclaw-gateway.service is OpenClaw-managed and excluded; coverage reported in the tick summary; lean v1 alerts on content_drift only (declared-registry + missing-deployment detection deferred). Run-mode exit-code contract: timer mode (default, this unit's ExecStart) always exits 0 — a scan fault is caught, recorded in `errors[]`, and reported as `ok:false` in the JSON summary, never a non-zero process exit (NFR-001); preflight/explicit mode (`--preflight`/`--once`) may exit 2 on a hard scan-inability fault (used by the deploy self-test). Finding drift itself is never a non-zero exit in either mode. Explicit non-goal: a pure verbal completion claim with no artifact and no assertion is not detectable (doctrine-only, FR-006 blind spot).

health_check.note: #891 — the prior endpoint had no grep filter and used journalctl's default output. Both halves were broken: journalctl writes '-- No entries --' to STDOUT with exit 0, so a deleted unit still read healthy (the probe accepted a systemd teardown line as the marker); and the default 'Aug 27 13:00:43' prefix does not parse as ISO-8601, so max_age_seconds was inert. `grep -F` makes the pipeline fail closed (exit 1 -> unknown, never a false healthy) and `-o short-iso` makes the leading token parseable. The window MUST be rolling, not calendar-day: the host is UTC and the timer fires at 13:00 UTC, so `--since today` is empty from 00:00 to 13:00 daily — with the grep filter added that is 13 hours of `unknown` and two WARN pages every morning. A 25h rolling window matches max_age_seconds and keeps the probe evaluable at every hour. This is the credential-liveness-probe idiom in full: its `--since '7 hours ago'` window and its 25200s bound agree with each other.

health_check.expected: status=success with exit_code=0 and completed_at_utc within the last 30h (24h cycle + 6h slack). exit_code here means the RUNNER EXECUTED CORRECTLY, not that the result was clean: drift_check exits 1 when it FINDS drift, which is a successful run, so that case records exit_code=0 with has_drift=true and is HEALTHY. Only a runner error (exit 2) records status=error. Drift itself is reported through the check's own output and alerting path, never through this liveness pointer.
health_check.note: #895 -- the component previously wrote no state at all; its only trace was /tmp/drift-check.log, which systemd-tmpfiles empties at every boot, so it could not be given a health check that was both honest and permitted (tests/canary/test_inventory_health_checks.py pins the set of components probing /tmp, owned by #894). The durable pointer is written on every exit path including early runner failures. has_drift is diagnostic and deliberately named to avoid the explicit-error scan keys.

services.name: backup-script-drift
services.purpose: Compares the repo copy scripts/office2/restic-backup.sh against the deployed /data/services/backup/scripts/backup.sh (kentonium3/kg-automation#903). #889 changed the repo copy with no manifest and the live file was installed by hand; they matched only by luck, on the one script the Tier-2 change-control guarantee depends on. OBSERVE-ONLY BY DESIGN: it never writes to /data/services/backup/scripts/, which must stay root-owned because it holds the NOPASSWD sudo target backup.sh -- a claude-writable directory on that path is equivalent to NOPASSWD: ALL, which was #899. Automating the install would reopen a fixed privilege escalation to save one manual command, so the install stays privileged and manual and this component makes divergence visible instead. Reads with O_NOFOLLOW and requires a regular file: a symlinked deployed copy is inconclusive, never match, because a deployed sudo target symlinked into claude's checkout is exactly the condition that must not be reported clean.

dependencies.description: Detects divergence between the repo's backup script and the copy actually executing on the host.
